pages.title: About Nathan
pages.summary: Adult psychiatric medication management in Texas, currently through LifeStance Health.

spans.text: Nathan Puls, PMHNP-BC, provides collaborative, evidence-based psychiatric care. He helps patients understand their symptoms and treatment options—not just leave with a prescription.
He provides adult medication management for anxiety, depression, ADHD, and related concerns. Nathan speaks English and Spanish and enjoys pickleball outside of work.
Appointment availability, insurance information, telehealth, office details, and patient resources are managed through LifeStance.

pages.title: My approach
pages.summary: Good psychiatric care starts with understanding the whole person, not just a list of symptoms or a diagnosis.

spans.text: I believe good psychiatric care starts with understanding the whole person, not just a list of symptoms or a diagnosis.

blocks.title: Listen First
blocks.text: Everyone has a unique story. I want to understand what you're experiencing, how it's affecting your life, and what matters most to you.

blocks.title: Keep It Simple
blocks.text: Mental health care doesn't have to be complicated. I'll explain diagnoses, medications, and treatment options clearly so you can make informed decisions.

blocks.title: Work Together
blocks.text: Treatment should be a conversation, not a set of instructions. We'll discuss your options and develop a plan that fits your needs and goals.

blocks.title: Look at the Full Picture
blocks.text: Mental health is connected to physical health, sleep, relationships, lifestyle, and life experiences. Medication can be helpful, but it's only one piece of the puzzle.

blocks.title: Make Thoughtful Changes
blocks.text: My goal isn't to prescribe more medication than necessary. It's to find the simplest effective treatment, make adjustments carefully, and regularly evaluate what's working.

pages.title: Your first visit
pages.summary: What to expect and how to prepare before we meet.

spans.text: I want your appointment to feel comfortable, straightforward, and productive. Here's what you should know before we meet.

I'm a psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner, which means I primarily focus on evaluating mental health concerns and managing medications. While our conversations may include supportive therapy, I don't provide traditional, ongoing talk therapy.
Please have the following information available:
Name, street address, and ZIP code.
A list of current medications, including doses (if not already provided).
Any psychiatric medications you've tried before and whether they helped.
What you'd most like help with.
We'll talk about your symptoms, medical history, lifestyle, and what you're hoping to accomplish. I'll explain my recommendations clearly, and we'll decide on a treatment plan together.
With your permission, I may use a secure recording or transcription tool to help document our conversation accurately. This allows me to focus more on listening and less on typing.

If we decide medication is appropriate, I'll send your prescription to your preferred pharmacy. We'll also discuss when to follow up, what to monitor, and how to contact the office if questions arise.

blocks.question: What's the process if I start a stimulant for ADHD?

spans.text: Depending on your circumstances and current practice policies, treatment may involve a urine drug screen, a telehealth visit with my supervising physician, and periodic in-person appointments. We will review the requirements that apply to your care.
Mornings from 9 am until noon are in-person or telehealth. Afternoons from 1 pm until 5 pm are telehealth.
